intent: Bring block_compulsive_opening.sh (705 lines) under the 250-line cap by moving its state, wrapper, install and reporting logic into four sourced libs, without changing behaviour and without breaking the already-installed app wrappers that hard-code the deployed script's path.
scope: install_all deploys the libs in the same commit, so there is no window where the deployed copy is split but its libs are missing
Non-goal: shell coverage for the new libs; no test suite exists for this script
changes: Split into four libs by concern: cco_state.sh (hour-bucket state files), cco_wrapper.sh (the launch gate), cco_install.sh (install/uninstall, the generated app wrapper and the pacman hook), cco_report.sh (status and help).

The entry script keeps its exact deployed path, /usr/local/bin/block-compulsive-opening.sh, and stays a real file there rather than a symlink. Already-installed app wrappers on disk hard-code that path, and the pacman hook at 96-restore-pkg-wrappers.hook invokes it; a symlink would also break dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" resolution.
_CCO_LIB_DIR probes for lib/ beside the script (repo tree) and falls back to the script's own directory (the flat /usr/local/bin deploy layout). Both branches are exercised below.

install_all copies the four libs flat into /usr/local/bin alongside the entry script, and uninstall_all removes them so no orphans are stranded. The copy runs even when the script is already at install_path, so a lib changed upstream still reaches the deployed copy that `rewrap-quiet` executes.
A guard before the source lines fails closed with an explicit message when any lib is unreadable, rather than dying on a bare `source` error.

Ran shfmt -w on the entry script, which removed a block of ~26 consecutive blank lines. No associative-array keys were affected: unlike install_leechblock.sh, this file's hyphenated keys ("signal-desktop") were already quoted, so the shfmt arithmetic-parsing bug does not apply here. Verified by grep after the run.

verification.evidence: Over-cap list went from 4 files to 3; block_compulsive_opening.sh no longer listed. All five files 182/238/149/120/102 lines, under 250.

verification.command: python3 line-multiset check of entry+4 libs against HEAD's block_compulsive_opening.sh
verification.evidence: MISSING functional lines: 0. Every non-comment, non-blank line from the pre-split file is accounted for across the five files.

verification.command: Heredoc body extraction and diff for all three heredocs
verification.evidence: This is the check verify_shell_split.sh cannot perform, because it cannot see inside a heredoc body. WRAPPER_EOF (5 lines, the generated app wrapper), HOOK_EOF (14 lines, the generated pacman hook) and EOF (26 lines, the help text) are each byte-identical between HEAD and the split. The two deployed artifacts this script generates are therefore provably unchanged.

Byte-identical output, both exit 0. The deployed copy is still the pre-split monolith and sha256-identical to HEAD, so this compares the split against the real pre-split behaviour rather than against itself. `help` differs only in the $0 invocation path, as expected.

verification.command: Flat-layout test: entry script + libs copied into one directory (the deployed shape)
verification.evidence: status runs correctly with exit 0, confirming the _CCO_LIB_DIR fallback branch works in the /usr/local/bin layout, not just the repo tree.

verification.command: Missing-lib guard: delete cco_report.sh from the flat layout and re-run
verification.evidence: Fails closed with 'Error: missing library cco_report.sh in <dir>' and exit code 1 (measured directly, not through a pipeline). A partially-deployed install cannot look successful to the pacman hook.

verification.command: shellcheck (no -x) + shfmt idempotence + bash -n on all five files
verification.evidence: shellcheck rc=0 with no suppressions; shfmt -w is a no-op on all five, so the pre-commit auto-format-and-re-stage cannot alter them; all five parse.

risks: The deployed copy at /usr/local/bin/block-compulsive-opening.sh is still the pre-split monolith and keeps working untouched; nothing breaks until someone runs `sudo block-compulsive-opening.sh install`, which now deploys the libs too. Verified that the pacman hook's `rewrap-quiet` path does not call install_all, so the hook cannot trigger a partial deploy.

The libs deploy flat into /usr/local/bin rather than into /usr/local/share/digital_wellbeing/lib. That is deliberate: install_leechblock_payload does an `rm -rf` mirror of the latter, which would delete these libs on the next pacman-wrapper install.
No test suite exists for this script, so coverage is 0% and the verification above is behavioural and textual rather than test-driven.
rollback: git revert this commit; block_compulsive_opening.sh returns to a single 705-line file and lib/cco_*.sh disappear.
If the split had already been deployed, re-run `sudo block-compulsive-opening.sh install` from the reverted tree to restore the monolith and remove the deployed libs.
Validate with: block-compulsive-opening.sh status (expect exit 0 and the per-app status table).
